title: TL-2000 Sting Sport: engine-mount crack, repair or replace
status: Completed · repair inspected and confirmed by the aircraft designer

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: A crack was found at a joint of the steel-tube engine mount.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: TL-2000 Sting Sport (2005), ROTAX 912.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: The crack was photographed in place before any work, to record its location and extent.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: Repair and replacement were weighed. The repair path was taken to the aircraft designer for review.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: The joint was weld-repaired.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: On 28 October 2025 an outside facility used wet fluorescent magnetic-particle inspection with a yoke to ASTM E1444. All four areas were accepted: the lower right and lower left diagonal weld toes and the bottom and left cross-tube heat-affected zones. On 8 December 2025 the aircraft designer confirmed in writing that the weldment is good and asked that the inspection protocol be added to the aircraft documentation.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: The NDT report and the designer's confirmation are kept with the aircraft records. The mount was refinished before reinstallation.

limits: Repair data and acceptance are specific to this aircraft and this finding.

title: Sling 2 / ROTAX 912 iS: qualifying an E-PROPS propeller with the airframe manufacturer
status: Engineering and manufacturer coordination substantially complete · awaiting Sling Aircraft manufacturer testing in South Africa · final approval pending

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: An owner wants an E-PROPS propeller on a Sling 2 with a ROTAX 912 iS. The airframe manufacturer's position decides whether that is an approved configuration.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: Sling 2 (also relevant to the Sling LSA / NGT family), ROTAX 912 iS, applicable E-PROPS DURANDAL-3 configuration.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: E-PROPS supplied technical package EP-2026-712 Rev A, DUR-3-175-C4-T configuration data and supporting EASA TCDS P.512, along with Sling-specific technical material and an offer of a propeller for testing.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: Instead of treating one installation as automatically approved, we asked for a configuration-level review.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: Lima Charlie Aero submitted the package to Sling's technical, airworthiness and engineering staff.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: Manufacturer testing by Sling Aircraft in South Africa is the next step; expected validation covers configuration, installation, weight and balance, pitch and RPM, vibration, performance, temperatures, fuel flow and a post-test inspection.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: The submittal and correspondence are kept with the job file.

title: TL-2000 Sting Sport / ROTAX 912: E-PROPS DURANDAL-3 engineering and installation control
status: Propeller-manufacturer engineering complete · installation and verification controlled by checklist

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: Fit an E-PROPS DURANDAL-3 to a specific TL-2000 / ROTAX 912 configuration with a controlled, documented process.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: TL-2000 Sting Sport, ROTAX 912 (80 hp), 2.27 gearbox and 175 cm DUR-3-175-C4-T propeller.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: E-PROPS engineering package EP-2026-398 includes the configuration data and an Engineering Compatibility Statement dated 31 March 2026.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: The review covered mass, inertia, operating limits, interfaces and vibration and torsional background. Airframe-manufacturer authorization through the LOA process is a separate gate.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: Criteria defined; installation not yet reported. The installation checklist calls for component identification, pre-installation inspection, torque of 24 N·m at the hub flange, 11 N·m at the hub clamp and 5 N·m at the spinner plate. Pitch is 23° with a blade-to-blade tolerance of ≤0.3°.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: Criteria defined; results not yet reported. The checklist specifies a ground run at 5,000–5,800 rpm, dynamic balance acceptance at ≤0.10 IPS with a ≤0.07 IPS target, and wide-open-throttle flight RPM of 5,500 ± 50. It also calls for post-installation re-torque and pitch checks.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: The checklist calls for weight and balance, equipment-list and logbook entries alongside the installation record.

title: Vashon Ranger R7 / Continental O-200-D: manufacturer-coordinated fuel evaluation
status: Evaluation submitted September 2026 · manufacturer disposition pending

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: An owner asked whether a controlled-specification automotive gasoline could be used in a Vashon Ranger R7 with a Continental O-200-D.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: Client aircraft baseline, fuel-system architecture, engine limitations and the existing approval gaps.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: An 11-page engineering evaluation covering detonation and preignition margin, vapor lock and hot-fuel behaviour, wetted-material compatibility, fuel density and metering, contamination and misfueling controls, placards and POH implications, instrumentation, a risk register and go/no-go decision gates.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: It treats two hazards separately: engine detonation suitability, and the installed aircraft's fuel-delivery and vapor margin. Passing one does not establish the other.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: The 11-page packet LCA-ENGINEERING-2026-006 Rev A was sent on 6 September 2026 to the aircraft owner and, at the same time, to the airframe manufacturer’s engineering staff and the engine manufacturer’s technical services.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: Manufacturer disposition pending. The evaluation's decision gates keep the two hazards separate: passing a detonation test does not establish the installed fuel-delivery and vapor margin.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: The packet, its data requests to the airframe and engine manufacturers and the follow-up correspondence are kept with the job file.

title: SeaRey (2002): return-to-service systems evaluation
status: Evaluation plan complete · inspection findings not yet reported

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: An amphibian returning to service after downtime: more than a routine annual or an engine-only check.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: 2002 SeaRey amphibian, ROTAX 912 UL, out of service since 2020.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: Six years without a current inspection: calendar-limited rubber, fuel left in the system and corrosion exposure all had to be assumed until checked.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: The plan crossed system boundaries: ROTAX calendar items, hoses and rubber, carburetors, fuel pump, cooling, gearbox, compression and leak-down, fuel contamination, propeller, corrosion and downtime effects, wing-attachment hardware, amphibious-airframe systems, records and inspection status, and sale readiness. With the wings already off, the plan used the opportunity to inspect the attachment hardware and the surrounding structure.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: The return-to-service scope was written and sent to the seller's broker before any work was quoted, so the aircraft was evaluated as a whole rather than as a routine annual.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: Compression and leak-down, fuel-system cleanliness, oil-system and gearbox condition, and attachment-hardware inspection are the planned gates.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: Findings and any return to service are recorded against that scope.

sources: Owner records: forensic compliance audit v2, 2026-09-21; PR #2 comment 6019840432

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: An aircraft whose maintenance claims could not be taken at face value: records had to be reconciled with the aircraft before any release decision.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: Flight Design CTSW, carbureted ROTAX 912, ballistic recovery system.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: A bulletin-by-bulletin audit against 54 manufacturer publications — 7 airframe safety alerts, 17 service bulletins, 6 service notifications and 24 ROTAX publications — with each claim traced to an entry, a document or a gap.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: Gaps and contradictions were separated from confirmed items: component identities, calendar and TBO status, gearbox applicability, carburetor float and circlip actions, rubber isolators, the recovery system and an inconsistency in the fuel-system record.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: A return-to-service plan of 144 traceable tasks with 6 hold points, configuration-verification steps, measured fuel-flow forms and an evidence register.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: Physical inspection and measurement against the hold points; the release decision follows the evidence, not the logbook alone.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: The audit report, compliance tracker and evidence requests are kept with the job file.

status: Records audit and return-to-service plan complete · physical inspection gates pending
